title: terraform: refactor private deployment modules (gpu node pools, iam, networking) + state layout and migration
author: Asha Patel
commits: Refactor: split private modules into gpu-node-pool, networking, iam (16f3b2e)
feat: add gpu node pool variable matrix for instance types and taints (9a6c1d4)
chore: introduce state layout split + migration helper (2b8d7a1)
test: add e2e plan checks for multi-env workspace (f4c9b0e)
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need clearer isolation between compute (GPU) concerns, networking, and IAM so customers can upgrade/scale node pools independently and so state is safer for multi-environment use. This PR reorganizes the Terraform modules used by the Private installer:

- Split modules: modules/gpu-node-pool (node pools + autoscaling + taints), modules/iam (service accounts, instance profiles, GPU-related policies), modules/networking (VPC, subnets, peering, route tables).
- Introduce modules/state-layout that proposes a per-environment/statefile split and includes a migration helper script to move legacy combined state into per-module statefiles.
- Add variable matrix for GPU instance types (p4d, a100, t4) and node tainting options to ensure scheduling for GPU workloads.
- Provide example terragrunt.hcl updates under examples/private-deploy to demonstrate workspace wiring for staging/prod.

Changes are backwards-compatible at apply time: the state migration is opt-in and guarded by the provided migration.sh script and detailed runbook. See release_notes for upgrade steps.

Testing: added terraform validate/plan checks for example configs; CI includes an "apply-dry-run" with mocked state to validate remote state layout changes. Initial CI run flagged formatting and a missing variable default — fixed in follow-up commit.

Notes: this PR touches state organization so extra review on the migration steps and lock handling is required. The migration script includes preflight checks (state lock, backup) and a verbose dry-run mode. The goal is to make future Private upgrades and per-module rollbacks predictable and auditable.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Important work — overall looks solid. Please expand the migration README with explicit `terraform state mv` examples and a note about Terraform v1.5 remote state locking semantics.
Asha Patel: Added examples and a lock-check step in migration.sh. Also added a short runbook section describing the ordering for networking -> iam -> compute.
Linus Chen: Can we ensure the IAM role ARNs are parameterized for on-prem vs cloud? Concerned about hardcoding service account names used by the installer.
Asha Patel: Updated modules/iam to accept `service_account_name` and `role_name_prefix` variables. Kept sensible defaults for cloud but allowed override for private/on-prem flows.

Priya Rao: CI plan shows a large delta for the networking module which will affect customers with existing peering. Confirmed that peering changes are no-op unless CIDR variables change. Added note to README.
Miguel Torres: Approving after migration runbook additions and a smoke e2e plan in staging. Left a minor nit about variable descriptions.
CI: terraform validate failed on first run (formatting). Fixed in commit 9a6c1d4 by running `terraform fmt` and adding fmt check to CI.
release_notes: Refactor private terraform modules: split GPU node pools, IAM, and networking modules; introduce state-layout module and migration helper. Breaking changes: none by default, requires opt-in migration for state (see modules/state-layout/README.md).
